definitions.explanation: An open area of land, typically covered with grass or wild plants; uncultivated land.

examples.japanese: {野|の}に{咲|さ}く{花|はな}は{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: Flowers blooming in the field are beautiful.
To walk through fields and mountains.
examples.notes: 野山 = fields and mountains, countryside

notes:
USAGE: {野|の} refers to open fields and wild areas. It's commonly used as a prefix meaning 'wild' or 'field-'.

AS A PREFIX (野〜 = wild):
・{野|の}ウサギ (wild rabbit)
・{野|の}バラ (wild rose)
・{野|の}イチゴ (wild strawberry)
・{野|の}{鳥|とり} (wild bird)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{野|の}{原|はら} (field, plain)
・{野|の}{山|やま} (fields and mountains)
・{平野|へいや} (plain)
・{野外|やがい} (outdoors, open-air)
・{分野|ぶんや} (field, area of study)
・{視野|しや} (field of vision)

NOTE: The character 野 has multiple readings: の (kun), や (on). In compounds it's often read や.
